speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by clarifying your timeline: have you noticed these gait and limb ataxia symptoms gradually over months, or did they appear suddenly? Also, have you experienced any recent changes in your vision or hearing?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That "drunk" appearance is concerning for cerebellar dysfunction. Have you experienced any recent headaches, nausea, or double vision alongside these motor symptoms? Also, do you have any history of diabetes, hypertension, or stroke?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, along with new-onset cerebellar ataxia, this is highly suspicious for JC virus reactivation. I am requesting an MRI of the brain with contrast to look for characteristic white matter lesions. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI. Please also confirm if you have noticed any weakness, numbness, or changes in sensation in your limbs.
